# Actual ChemDraw arrow exchange captures

These files were saved through the GUI of ChemDraw 26.0.0.6599 on macOS 26.5.1
arm64 on 2026-09-29. File hashes and capture conditions are in
[provenance.json](provenance.json). They are immutable external application
outputs, not expected results generated by ReShiki's decoder.

- `numeric-before.cdxml`: the transformed mixed drawing copied from ReShiki to
  ChemDraw. Its seven atoms, six bonds, caption, group and rectangle survived;
  the arrow was invisible and absent from the saved file.
- `numeric.cdx` and `numeric.cdxml`: the same native source exported with the
  caption compatibility correction, then changed at exactly one binary object
  tag from `0x8027` to `0x8021`. ChemDraw opened and displayed the arrow, and the
  operator saved both files through its GUI. Bounds-only and axis-only variants
  did not restore the arrow. These diagnostic files establish the tag's meaning.
- `reaction-source.rsk`: the frozen native reaction-shortcut result containing
  ethanol and two ethylamine molecules, two forward arrows and two native
  reaction-role records.
- `reaction.cdx` and `reaction.cdxml`: the native reaction drawing copied into
  ChemDraw using a rebuilt ReShiki application with the corrected arrow tag.
  Both arrows were visible. These full files were then saved through ChemDraw's
  GUI before the import fill-enumeration fix. The uncorrected reader rejected
  their ordinary arrows as filled; the corrected reader imports the whole
  drawing.
- `numeric-final.*` and `reaction-final.*`: final actual ReShiki clipboard pastes
  saved through ChemDraw's GUI as CDX/CDXML. `numeric-clipboard-return.rsk` and
  `reaction-clipboard-return.rsk` were saved through ReShiki after copying those
  complete drawings back from ChemDraw's native clipboard. Both directions
  passed. The numeric status bar visibly disclosed the metadata limitation.
- The two `*-clipboard-audit.json` files compare connectivity, coordinates,
  groups and drawing objects after one global translation. The independent
  RDKit identities are recorded separately in `independent-identities.json`.

The saved binaries use arrow object `0x8021`, and `FillType=None` is property
`0x0a37` with payload `01 00`. ChemDraw adds a legacy graphic linked through
`SupersededBy`; the numeric file also includes automatically generated reaction
scheme and step references. All arrowhead parameters remain `600`, `525`, `150`
(6 pt length, 0.125 notch, 1.5 pt half-width). The reaction's three molecular
components remain `CCO`, `CCN`, `CCN`, with combined formula `C6H20N2O` and
InChIKey `VOQVNJWELYGUNW-UHFFFAOYSA-N`.

The binary constants are independently corroborated by the published
[CambridgeSoft/Revvity CDX constants](https://github.com/Glysade/chemdraw/blob/5dd743230d75ecacacdf8dcd0b0e022f13173b9c/chemdraw/CDXConstants.h#L569)
and its [fill enumeration](https://github.com/Glysade/chemdraw/blob/5dd743230d75ecacacdf8dcd0b0e022f13173b9c/chemdraw/CDXConstants.h#L1017).
Only format facts were used; no implementation source was copied. The older
SDK overview's erroneous arrow tag was also identified in
[Roger Sayle's 2013 ACS presentation](https://www.nextmovesoftware.com/talks/Sayle_FileFormats_ACS_201309.pdf).

The vendor's [reaction-step property definitions](https://chemapps.stolaf.edu/iupac/cdx/sdk/ReactionStep.htm)
distinguish arrows, atom-map pairs, pluses, reactants/products, and above/below-arrow
objects. The native validator checks these target categories. These captures
establish valid references to a legacy arrow graphic, a drawing group and a
standalone caption. Synthetic regressions additionally cover fragment and caption
reactants/products, explicit arrow targets, atom pairs, plus captions/symbols,
and rejection of objects of the wrong kind. The stricter target checks were added
after the desktop capture; both genuine numeric captures are reimported unchanged
by the final regression suite.
The [vendor Arrow_Type definition](https://chemapps.stolaf.edu/iupac/cdx/sdk/properties/Arrow_Type.htm)
also permits `NoHead` and an omitted arrow type. Native-import positives cover
both forms as editable line graphics referenced by `ReactionStepArrows`.

The reaction test exercises full CDX and CDXML engine imports, molecular
identity, endpoints, stroke and head sizes. The numeric tests cover the binary
codec, arrow reader and complete CDXML import with an explicit metadata warning.
Full mixed-drawing binary clipboard verification also includes the
[caption compatibility fix](https://github.com/Ameyanagi/ReShiki/pull/79).
External reaction roles and ReShiki transform depth are not established by these
checks. Preserve the native `.rsk` document for those editor-specific records.
